seg.seg_note: Four segments: Life Sciences, Diagnostics, Dental, Environmental & Applied Solutions (+ Other = unallocated corporate). Releases in this period carry no segment table; segment sales/OP from the 10-Q segment note and depreciation, amortization and growth from the 10-Q MD&A segment sections (three-month columns). Total/segment growth tables in this period are presented as components that sum to total growth (core + acquisitions + currency = total); acq and fx are stored with the sign flipped to the 'less the impact of' convention used from Q3-17 onward (core = total + acq + fx). Release labels: 'Core (non-GAAP)' 2.0, 'Acquisitions (non-GAAP)' 6.0, 'Impact of currency translation (non-GAAP)' (1.5) (six months: 2.5 / 5.5 / (1.5), total 6.5). Dental has an 'Acquisitions and other' row of '—'. Diagnostics Q2-17 OP includes the $76m restructuring/impairment charge for discontinuing a molecular diagnostics product line. Recurring revenue % not disclosed.

FY2017: GAAP diluted EPS $3.16-$3.23; adjusted diluted EPS raised to $3.90-$3.97 (from $3.85-$3.95) (pretax amortization $0.93 / $654.8m pretax, $520.6m after-tax; Q2 restructuring $0.11; tax effect ($0.22); YTD discrete tax ($0.08)).
ngaap.notes: Adjusted diluted EPS from continuing ops (non-GAAP) adds back pretax amortization of acquisition-related intangibles (tax-effected in the aggregate 'Tax effect' line) plus gains/charges deemed non-recurring (sale of investments, restructuring plans fundamentally different from ongoing DBS productivity, acquisition-related items, early extinguishment of debt) and discrete tax items. From 2017 (ASU 2016-09) equity-compensation excess tax benefits above ~$10m/quarter anticipated are excluded. No adjusted operating profit or margin is published. Item after-tax amounts are from the release footnotes. Q2-17 adds back the $76m restructuring/impairment charge (inside operating costs, no separate IS line). Equity-comp excess tax benefits approximated the anticipated $10m (no adjustment). No free cash flow table in the release.
